textbookText: Kingdom protista is further divided into 3 groups: Group A: Photosynthetic protists Group B: Consumer-decomposer protists Group C: Protozoan protists
1. Group A: Photosynthetic protists They can furher be divided into three phyla:

Phylum 1: Pyrrophyta i. They are aquatic, mostly found in marine water; commonly called dinoflagellates. ii. They are unicellular, motile, and photosynthetic. iii. Some of them are bio-luminiscent glowing in dark because of presence of phosphorescence. Example: Noctiluca iv. Body is externally covered by theca or lorica. v. They reproduce only by asexual method.

Example: Noctiluca, Gymnodinium Phylum 2: Chrysophyta i. They are unicellular and some occur in colonial form, found mostly in marine water. ii. Their cell body is covered by hard siliceous shell called frustula. iii. Reproduction takes place by sexually and asexually both. Binary fission is common. iv. They include diatoms and golden brown algae. Diatoms are important food source to animals. Example: Navicula, Triceratum

Phylum 3: Euglenophyta i. They are motile, free living flagellate protists found in freshwater and damp soil. ii. Their body shape is maintained by plasma membrane and pellicle. iii. They move with the help of flagella. iv. Some of them have chlorophyll and are photosynthetic. Their reserve food is called Paramylum. v. Near the base of flagellum lies light sensitive spot called eye spot.
vi. They behave as both plants and animals hence show mixotrophic mode of nutrition. vii. They reproduce asexually by longitudinal binary fission. Example: Euglena, Peranema, Trachelomonus

2. Group B: Cosumer decomposer protists or slime moulds i. These organisms are also called protistan fungi as they resemble both amoeboid protozoans and fungi. ii. They don’t have chlorophyll and hence can’t produce their own food. They derive their food from decaying organic matter. iii. They reproduce by sexually and asexually both.

They are of two types Type 1. Plasmodial or true or acellular slime moulds i. They are found in decaying leaves and wooden log. ii. Their outer covering is plasma membrane. iii. They are free living irregular shaped mass of slimy protoplasm. iv. Their vegetative stage is called Plasmodium, represented by a large sized multinucleated structure. Example: Tubifera, Physarum

Type 2. Cellular slime moulds i. Cellular slime moulds are found on upper layer of moist soil rich in decaying organic matter. ii. Their feeding stage is single-celled amoeboid stage. iii. When there is scarcity off food, they aggregate but retain their individuality and reproduce by spore formation. Example: Dictyostelium, Acytostelium

3. Group C: Protozoan protists i. They are aquatic and terrestrial both. Most of them are parasitic. Some of them are either free living of commensal or saprophytic. ii. They are simplest, primitive, acellular and microscopic animalcules. iii. They are solitary or colonial having protoplasmic body organization. iv. Body is covered by cell membrane, pellicle and shells. v. They have varied body shape such as spherical, oval, elongated and flattened.

vi. Cytoplasm is differentiated into ectoplasm and endoplasm. vii. Number and shape of nucleus also vary among protozoans. viii. Nutrition is holozoic and digestion is intracellular. ix. Respiration takes place by diffusion through general body surface. x. Excretion also occurs through general body surface or through cell anus (cytopyge). xi. Amount of salt and water in the body is maintained by contractile vacuole. The process is called osmoregulation. xii. Reproduction takes place by asexually and sexually both. Asexual reproduction by fission, budding, or sporulation and sexual reproduction by gamete formation. xiii. Encystment usually occurs in unfavourable condition.
Protozoan protists can be divided into four classes on the basis of their locomotory organelles:

Class 1: Flagellata or mastigophora i. Body is externally covered by Pellicle. ii. Their locomotion takes place through flagella. iii. They have single nucleus. iv. They are either free living or parasitic.

Class 2: Rhizopoda or Sarcodina i. Body is irregular shaped and externally bounded by plasma membrane. ii. They have pseudopodia for locomotion. iii. They are solitary, free living or parasitic. iv. Asexual reproduction takes place by fission.
Class 3: Sporozoa i. Their body is externally covered by pellicle. ii. They reproduce asexually and sexually. iii. They are endoparasites.
iv. They have no locomotory organelles. Examples: Plasmodium, Babesia, Monocystis etc
